# 2005B Question 16 {.unnumbered}

::: {.exam-question}
## Question {.question-label}

[**Explain**]{.task-verb} the changes on Functional Residual Capacity (FRC) that take place with administration of anaesthesia.
:::

:::: {#answer-structure}

## Suggested Structure

[**Explain**]{.task-verb} the size and time course of the FRC change using its determinants. Link posture, muscle tone and diaphragm shape to the mechanism, then consider pre-existing conditions, surgery, regional anaesthesia and PEEP.

::: {.structure-headings}
### Definition and Determinants

### Size and Time Course During General Anaesthesia

### Posture, Muscle Tone and Diaphragm Shape

### Patient and Surgical Factors

### Regional Anaesthesia and PEEP
:::

::::

## Examiner Comments

::: {.examiner-comments}
**48 %** of candidates passed this question.

Points required for a pass were:

- Understanding the determinants of FRC
- The size and time course of the change with general anaesthesia
- Explanation of the causes of the change (posture, muscle tone, diaphragm shift)

Additional marks were given for:

- Changes in the shape of the diaphragm
- The exaggerated effects caused by abdominal surgery, and pre-existing conditions
- Loss of nitrogen splinting, chest wall compliance vs. lung compliance
- Differences with local /regional anaesthesia
- PEEP
- Intrathoracic blood volume
- The effects of the FRC change

Many candidates described the results/consequences of the (anaesthetic-induced) change in FRC, which did not attract many additional marks.
:::
